threads_text: Jensen Huang made his first trip to Kazakhstan and told it to stop just exporting energy and start exporting intelligence. NVIDIA also backed Higgsfield, the $5.4 billion AI video startup with most of its engineers there. Could a country you rarely hear about become Europe's AI factory?
caption:
NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang made his first visit to Kazakhstan on October 23 and called it a future AI factory hub for all of Europe.
His pitch: turn energy into intelligence and export that instead.
The same day, NVIDIA joined the funding of AI video startup Higgsfield, which keeps most of its engineers in Kazakhstan.

Which country do you think becomes the next big AI hub?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

site_article.seo_title: Jensen Huang in Kazakhstan: NVIDIA backs Higgsfield, AI hub plans
site_article.seo_description: On his first visit to Kazakhstan, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang called it a future AI hub for Europe as NVIDIA invested in AI video startup Higgsfield.
site_article.answer_summary: Jensen Huang visited Kazakhstan for the first time on October 23, 2026, and said the country could export AI computing instead of only energy. NVIDIA also invested in Higgsfield, an AI video startup with most of its engineers in Kazakhstan.
site_article.hero_alt: A man in a black leather jacket touring an AI center with officials.

paragraphs.text: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang made his first visit to Kazakhstan on October 23, 2026, traveling to the capital, Astana, at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiyev, who also serves as the minister of artificial intelligence and digital development. According to The Astana Times, Huang toured the alem.ai International AI Center and joined Madiyev for a fireside chat, an appearance that closed the country's national AI Month program.

Huang also met President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev at the Akorda presidential palace, where Tokayev awarded him the Order of Dostyk, First Class, The Times of Central Asia reported. Tokayev noted that the government had declared 2026 the Year of Digitalization and Artificial Intelligence. Huang told the Astana audience that Kazakhstan was the first country he had visited where the president had declared it an AI nation.

The central theme of the visit was energy. Huang argued that Kazakhstan has a basic advantage in its natural resources and suggested that, rather than only exporting energy, the country could convert it into intelligence and export that. Qazinform reported that he named electricity, data and demand for AI products as the three ingredients the industry needs. CNBC reported that Huang described Kazakhstan as a future computing and AI factory hub for all of Europe.

Huang also said that countries building their own large language models is a matter of national security, and he praised the national model, Kazakh LLM, according to The Astana Times and Qazinform. He pointed to physical AI in mining, agriculture, logistics and energy as an area where the country could specialize.

Several hardware projects were presented during the visit. The Astana Times reported that the national operator Kazakhtelecom has deployed 880 NVIDIA GPUs in Astana and Almaty and plans more than 2,000 additional GPUs in 2027, including over 1,000 Vera Rubin processors in the Ekibastuz region. US company Firebird signed an investment agreement with the government and holds a US export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs, with a first phase at the Data Center Valley site in Ekibastuz expected to begin commercial operations in the third quarter of 2027.

On the same day, Higgsfield, a San Francisco based AI video and image generation company, announced that NVIDIA and the investment firm TCV had joined an extension of its Series B round. The amounts were not disclosed. The round builds on a $400 million raise led by DST Global in August that valued the company at $5.4 billion, according to The Astana Times. Higgsfield was cofounded by Alex Mashrabov and Kazakh entrepreneur Yerzat Dulat and keeps most of its engineering team in Kazakhstan.

In its announcement, Higgsfield said it passed $1 billion in annualized revenue run rate in September, 18 months after launch, and that it has more than 40 million users, with the United States as its largest market. Those figures come from the company and were not independently verified. Huang described the investment in terms of the team, telling the audience in Astana that investors should back people rather than companies.

For NVIDIA, the trip fits a pattern of courting governments that want their own AI computing capacity. Countries with abundant energy can offer what data center builders need most, and every new national cluster is a potential buyer of NVIDIA hardware. The Higgsfield deal gives the visit a consumer face, since the startup sells AI video tools mainly to creators and brands, with the United States as its biggest market.

The next marker is Firebird's first phase at Data Center Valley, which is scheduled to start commercial operations in the third quarter of 2027 and will show whether the export licenses turn into working capacity.
